relations.subject: cloud/guides/javascript-udfs
relations.evidence: User-defined functions written in JavaScript support the [ECMAScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECMAScript) standard, with some restrictions and extensions. For more information, see [JavaScript Functions for Query Reference](../javascript-udfs/javascript-functions-with-couchbase.md).

relations.subject: js-udf:inline-function
relations.evidence: An inline SQL++ function is a user-defined function that executes a SQL++ expression. The SQL++ expression is stored internally by the Query Service. For more information, see [Create an Inline User-Defined Function](create-user-defined-function.md#create-inline).

relations.subject: js-udf:sql-managed-udf
relations.evidence: A SQL++ managed JavaScript function is a user-defined function that executes a JavaScript function. The JavaScript function is stored internally by the Query Service. You do not need to create a JavaScript library to create and use SQL++ managed JavaScript functions.

relations.subject: js-udf:sql-managed-udf
relations.evidence: If you create a user-defined function this way, you cannot group related functions or change access restrictions for multiple related functions at once.

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.evidence: To create a JavaScript library function, you must first create a JavaScript library and add JavaScript functions to that library. For more information, see [Create a JavaScript Library](create-javascript-library.md).

relations.subject: js-udf:external-function
relations.evidence: After you create your user-defined functions, you can call them like any other SQL++ function. For more information, see [Call a User-Defined Function](call-user-defined-function.md).
